paraphrase: Homage to the stainless ocean of consciousness named Śiva, whose waves and bubbles are the appearance of the mass of thirty-six principles (tattvas).
speaker: Śivayogi Śivācārya (author)
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: यस्योर्मिबुद्बुदाभासः षट्त्रिंशत्तत्त्वसञ्चयः । निर्मलं शिवनामानं तं वन्दे चिन्महोदधिम् ॥ ३ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: The author's lineage: a famed Śivayogin foremost among those perfect in conduct; in his line the ācārya Muddadeva; his son the Śivācārya Siddhanātha, 'crest-jewel of the Vīraśaivas', from whose ācārya-family good conduct and steady Śiva-devotion were born; his son Śivayogi, named for his experience of Śiva in the supreme sky of consciousness-bliss, who protected Śiva-devotion against the counter-doctrines of the Buddha and others and set the Vīraśaiva path of dharma in motion.
speaker: Śivayogi Śivācārya (author)
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: Having studied the Śaiva tantras from the Kāmika to the Vātula and all the Śaiva Purāṇas, he composed the work without conflict with the Vedic path, to establish distinguished conduct, to refute wrong paths and to delight the discerning — the whole wealth of the Vīraśaivas, untouched by faults.
speaker: Śivayogi Śivācārya (author)
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: This teaching was spoken of old by the god to the Goddess and to Nandin in all the Āgamas and Purāṇas; Reṇuka, lord of gaṇas, perfected in that lineage, told it again on earth to Agastya — the great Vīraśaiva tantra of one hundred and one sthalas, called Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi because it is the highest of all Śaiva tantras.
speaker: Śivayogi Śivācārya (author)
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: Asked by Brahmā, Śambhu emitted the pramathas, equal to himself in splendour, all-pervading and all-powerful, their minds flooded with awakened bliss, able to create and dissolve worlds; among them Reṇuka and Dāruka were dear to Śiva.
speaker: narrator
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: Called by Śiva to receive tāmbūla, Reṇuka in his excitement leapt over Dāruka; Śiva rebuked him: overstepping my devotees destroys life, fortune, family and fame — as Yama, Viṣṇu, Dakṣa and Kāla learned when they slighted Mārkaṇḍeya, Bhṛgu, Dadhīci, the gaṇas and Śveta; since you have thoughtlessly overstepped my devotee Dāruka, be born on earth.
speaker: narrator
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: Śiva to Reṇuka: north of Śrīśaila in the Triliṅga country is the great village Kollipāki; from my liṅga named Someśvara dwelling there you will appear without touching the human state; you will establish on earth the śāstra devoted to my non-duality, agreeing with Veda and Vedānta, for the good of all, and proclaim my glory and my devotees' according to the Vedic path.
speaker: Śiva
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: In the Triliṅga country, in the town called Kollipāki, Reṇuka appeared from the great liṅga Someśvara.
speaker: narrator; Reṇuka (Revaṇa)
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: अथ त्रिलिङ्गविषये कोल्लिपाक्यभिधे पुरे । सोमेश्वरमहालिङ्गात् प्रादुरासीत् स रेणुकः ॥ १ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: Reṇuka to the astonished people: for a certain reason I have come here from Śiva's liṅga; my name is Reṇukasiddha, leader of the lineage of siddhas, moving freely in this world as protector of the Śiva-siddhānta and refuting the false scriptures of the Jainas, Cārvākas, Bauddhas and others.
speaker: narrator; Reṇuka (Revaṇa)
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: केनचित् कारणेनाहं शिवलिङ्गादिहाभवम् । नाम्ना रेणुकसिद्धोऽहं सिद्धसन्ताननायकः ॥ ११ ॥ स्वच्छन्दचारी लोकेऽस्मिन् शिवसिद्धान्तपालकः । खण्डयन् जैनचार्वाकबौद्धादीनां दुरागमान् ॥ १२ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: Many siddhāntas are renowned, differing in conduct and meaning according to taste — Sāṃkhya, Yoga, Pāñcarātra, the Vedas and Pāśupata — and are not to be struck down by argument; the Veda is chief among them and they are authoritative by following it; Pāñcarātra, Sāṃkhya and Yoga follow part of the Veda, while the Śaiva is made of the Veda and excels because it follows the whole Veda; the Śaiva tantra called Siddhānta, spoken by Śiva, is always authoritative like the Veda.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: The Śaiva tantra is fourfold — vāma (centred on Śakti), dakṣiṇa (Bhairava), miśra (the seven Mothers) and siddhānta; the Siddhānta Āgama is Veda-consonant because it teaches Vedic dharma and opposes those outside the Veda; Veda and Siddhānta are one because they teach one meaning, and their authority is equal.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: In the great tantra called Siddhānta, beginning with the Kāmika and spoken by Śiva, the supreme Vīraśaiva doctrine is taught in the later portion (uttara-bhāga).
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: सिद्धान्ताख्ये महातन्त्रे कामिकाद्ये शिवोदिते । निर्दिष्टमुत्तरे भागे वीरशैवमतं परम् ॥ १४ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: Because they delight especially in knowledge (vidyā) whose form is Śiva, these fortunate ones are called Vīraśaivas; the syllable 'vī' denotes the knowledge that awakens the oneness of Śiva and the jīva, and the Śaivas who delight (ramante) in it are held to be Vīraśaivas.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: विद्यायां शिवरूपायां विशेषाद् रमणं यतः । तस्मादेते महाभागा वीरशैवा इति स्मृताः ॥ १५ ॥ वीशब्देनोच्यते विद्या शिवजीवैक्यबोधिका । तस्यां रमन्ते ये शैवा वीरशैवास्तु ते मताः ॥ १६ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: One who delights in (Śiva-)knowledge and keeps away māyā, which is to be abandoned, as one keeps away a dog, is by this derivation called Vīramāheśvara; the knowledge born of Vedānta is vidyā, and one who delights in it is called vīra.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: विद्यायां रमते यस्मान्मायां हेयां श्ववद् रहेत् । अनेनैव निरुक्तेन वीरमाहेश्वरः स्मृतः ॥ १७ ॥ वेदान्तजन्यं यज्ज्ञानं विद्येति परिकीत्यते । विद्यायां रमते तस्यां वीर इत्यभिधीयते ॥ १८ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: Śaivas and Māheśvaras are not ultimately different: those devoted to the sacrifice of knowledge (worship within) are Śaivas, those devoted on earth to the sacrifice of action are Māheśvaras; therefore Śaivas should worship within and Māheśvaras without.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: यथा तथा न भिद्यन्ते शैवा माहेश्वरा अपि । शिवाश्रितेषु ते शैवा ज्ञानयज्ञरता नराः ॥ २० ॥ माहेश्वराः समाख्याताः कर्मयज्ञरता भुवि । तस्मादभ्यन्तरे कुर्युः शैवा माहेश्वरा बहिः ॥ २१ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: The Vīraśaivas are of six kinds according to the difference in the dharma of the sthalas, named bhakta and so on by those who have mastered the śāstra; the śāstra of the Vīraśaivas is sixfold by the sthalas, by the conjunction of their dharmas, and by the difference of qualified aspirants (adhikārin).
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: वीरशैवास्तु षड्भेदाः स्थलधर्मविभेदतः । भक्तादिव्यवहारेण प्रोच्यन्ते शास्त्रपारगैः ॥ २२ ॥ शास्त्रं तु वीरशैवानां षड्विधं स्थलभेदतः । धर्मभेदसमायोगादधिकारिविभेदतः ॥ २३ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: One in whom devotion to Śiva has arisen is called a bhakta; the teaching of the dharmas he is to practise is the bhakta-sthala.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: शैवी भक्तिः समुत्पन्ना यस्यासौ भक्त उच्यते । तस्यानुष्ठेयधर्माणां मुक्तिर्भक्तस्थलं मतम् ॥ २६ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: The fifteen sub-sthalas of the bhakta-sthala: embodiment fit for the path (piṇḍa), knowledge of the embodied self (piṇḍajñāna), rejection of saṃsāra, initiation, wearing the liṅga, wearing ash, wearing rudrākṣa, repeating the five-syllable mantra, the practice of the devotee's path, worship of guru and liṅga, worship of the jaṅgama, receiving the prasāda of these, and the three gifts — with a purpose, without a purpose, and innate.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: Śiva is without conceptual distinction, formless, attributeless and beyond the world; through connection with beginningless ignorance a part of him is named jīva; Śiva abides in the self as water in the moonstone, fire in the sunstone and the sprout in the seed.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: The Cārvākas call the body the self, others the senses, the Bauddhas the intellect; but the self is none of these, being known through the cognition 'I' and through memory of what was experienced; one who discerns the eternal self as distinct from body, senses and intellect, and the Lord as the impeller distinct from the selves, is called piṇḍajñānin.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: For one whose heart is cleansed and who discerns the eternal from the non-eternal, the resolve to abandon saṃsāra arises: who that discerns would want fleeting pleasures from son and wife, or a heaven that perishes, when even Viṣṇu met death in his births as fish, tortoise, boar, man-lion and man? Born by karma into castes beginning with brāhmaṇa, the creature burns in the fire of the threefold suffering — bodily-mental, from beings, and from the gods.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: The disciple — discerning, dispassionate, pure-minded, seeking — approaches a guru who is renowned, free of greed and delusion, skilled in inquiry into the self, knower of the Śiva-siddhānta with doubts cut, versed in all tantric practice, righteous and truthful, of hereditary good conduct, avoiding wrong ways, devoted to meditation on Śiva, peaceful, expert in ash and tripuṇḍra, wearing rudrākṣa and the liṅga, devoted to liṅga worship, knowing the yoga of liṅga and aṅga, with a firm disposition toward non-duality.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: With water from pots consecrated by the five brahma-mantras the ācārya and his assistants bathe the disciple three times; then the guru utters the Śaiva five-syllable mantra, which carries one across the fear of saṃsāra, secretly into his right ear, with its metre, form, seer, deity and the method of placing it on the body.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: The guru takes one liṅga — of crystal, of mountain stone, of moonstone, a bāṇa, or of sunstone — purified, set on its seat, bathed and worshipped with scents and flowers, installs it single-mindedly in the disciple's life-breath (prāṇa), and places it in the disciple's hand.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: This is your prāṇaliṅga, to be borne like your breath; never at any time or place separate it from your body.
speaker: the guru (within Reṇuka's teaching)
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: प्राणवद्धारणीयं तत्प्राणलिङ्गमिदं तव । कदाचित्कुत्रचिद्वापि न वियोजय देहतः ॥ २६ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: If through carelessness the liṅga falls from the body to the ground, the verse tells the disciple to give up his life at once, for the attainment of liberation.
speaker: the guru (within Reṇuka's teaching)
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse. Restricted: recorded as the text's statement of the gravity of losing the liṅga, not as a practice; wording of the verse deliberately omitted.

paraphrase: Wearing the liṅga is twofold, outer and inner; holding in the mind the supreme liṅga of consciousness, Śaṅkara's, the cause of all, is the inner — the supreme principle called Śiva, consciousness itself, cause of the universe, rid of the world's impurity, partless, free of conceptual construction, the upsurge of being and bliss, immeasurable, indescribable, worshipped by those who seek liberation.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: In the base (mūlādhāra), in the heart and between the brows of all embodied beings the liṅga of light (jyotirliṅga) always shines, which the Āgamas call brahman.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: मूलाधारे च हृदये भ्रूमध्ये सर्वदेहिनाम् । ज्योतिर्लिङ्गं सदा भाति यद् ब्रह्मेत्याहुरागमाः ॥ ३५ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: The liṅga is the unlimited, unmanifest, eternal brahman, delimited within by its own māyā for the sake of worship; that in which this moving and unmoving world dissolves and from which it arises again and again is the eternal liṅga-brahman — therefore it is called liṅga, of the nature of being, bliss and consciousness, and called brahman for its vastness and expanding.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: Continuous contemplation of the liṅga of light at the base, in the heart or between the brows is the inner wearing of the liṅga; the yogin should visualize it gold-coloured at the base, coral-red in the heart and crystal-clear between the brows; this inner wearing, free of limiting adjuncts, is a crore times better than wearing the outer liṅga.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: Those who bear the lordly liṅga of consciousness in the heart do not return to the terrible round of saṃsāra; contemplation of the inner liṅga, effort in self-knowledge and the power of serving the guru are the causes of liberation; yogins endowed with dispassion and knowledge, with steady minds, lose their taste for the outer.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: Whether one is able to bear the liṅga inwardly or not, one should also wear the outer liṅga, knowing with certainty that it is of that same form.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: अन्तर्धारयितुं लिङ्गमशक्तः शक्त एव वा । बाह्यं च धारयेल्लिङ्गं तद्रूपमिति निश्चयात् ॥ ४८ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: The liṅga is threefold — gross, subtle and beyond the highest: the gross is this iṣṭaliṅga worn outwardly on the body; the subtle is this prāṇaliṅga, made of inner contemplation; that called beyond the highest is named the liṅga of fulfilment (tṛptiliṅga).
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse. The third member is named tṛptiliṅga here; the vacana tradition calls it bhāvaliṅga (see SSM 15.37–44 for bhāvaliṅga as a liṅga-sthala).

original.text: लिङ्गं तु त्रिविधं प्रोक्तं स्थूलं सूक्ष्मं परात्परम् । इष्टलिङ्गमिदं स्थूलं यद् बाह्ये धार्यते तनौ ॥ ४९ ॥ प्राणलिङ्गमिदं सूक्ष्मं यदन्तर्भावनामयम् । परात्परं तु यत्प्रोक्तं तृप्तिलिङ्गं तदुच्यते ॥ ५० ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: The Lord's liṅga may be worn on the head, the throat, the armpit, the chest, the belly or in the hand; wearing it below the navel is a cause of sin, and it is not to be worn at the tip of matted hair, on the lower back or in an unclean place.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: मूर्ध्नि वा कण्ठदेशे वा कक्षे वक्षःस्थलेऽपि वा । कुक्षौ हस्तस्थले वापि धारयेल्लिङ्गमैश्वरम् ॥ ५२ ॥ नाभेरधस्ताल्लिङ्गस्य धारणं पापकारणम् । जटाग्रे त्रिकभागे च मलस्थाने न धारयेत् ॥ ५३ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: The liṅga-wearer, always pure and collected, should worship his own lovely liṅga with scents, flowers and the like on the seat of his palm (karapīṭha); this palm-worship is better than worship on an outer pedestal, for all Vīraśaivas who seek liberation, always.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: लिङ्गधारी सदा शुद्धो निजलिङ्गं मनोरमम् । अर्चयेद् गन्धपुष्पाद्यैः करपीठे समाहितः ॥ ५४ ॥ बाह्यपीठार्चनादेतत् करपीठार्चनं वरम् । सर्वेषां वीरशैवानां मुमुक्षूणां निरन्तरम् ॥ ५५ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: Wearing the liṅga is declared for the Vīraśaiva in the Vedas, śāstras, Purāṇas and the Āgamas beginning with the Kāmika; the Ṛk says 'Your purifier is spread out, O Brahmaṇaspati' — therefore that purifying Śaiva liṅga is to be worn; 'brahman' names the liṅga and its lord is Īśvara, and the body is pure by contact with it; the 'unheated body' is the ignorant, the unripe, one without the sacraments and without initiation, who cannot attain the supreme liṅga.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse. Interprets Ṛgveda 9.83.1 (src:rgveda).

paraphrase: Ash has five names — vibhūti, bhasita, bhasma, kṣāra and rakṣā — for five reasons: vibhūti because it causes prosperity, bhasita because it makes the principle shine, bhasma because it reproaches sins, kṣāra because it makes calamities flow away.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: विभूतिर्भसितं भस्म क्षारं रक्षेति भस्मनः । एतानि पञ्चनामानि हेतुभिः पञ्चभिर्भृशम् ॥ ४ ॥ विभूतिर्भूतिहेतुत्वाद् भसितं तत्त्वभासनात् । पापानां भर्त्सनाद्भस्म क्षरणात् क्षारमापदाम् ॥ ५ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: Bathing with ash is the supreme 'fire-bath', chief among baths and removing impurity; for those who bathe in ash daily the water-baths are unnecessary; the fire-bath with ash is enjoined for ascetics.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: When the three-eyed lord of the worlds, at the destruction of the Triple City, looked with open eyes, many drops of water fell from his eyes; from them the rudrākṣas were born.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: पुरा त्रिपुरसंहारे त्रिनेत्रो जगतां पतिः । उदपश्यत् पुरां योगमुन्मीलितविलोचनः ॥ ४७ ॥ निपेतुस्तस्य नेत्रेभ्यो बहवो जलबिन्दवः । तेभ्यो जाता हि रुद्राक्षा रुद्राक्षा इति कीर्तिताः ॥ ४८ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: Whether brāhmaṇa or outcaste, fool or learned, one is freed from all sins simply by wearing rudrākṣa.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: ब्राह्मणो वान्त्यजो वापि मूर्खो वा पण्डितोऽपि वा । रुद्राक्षधारणादेव मुच्यते सर्वपातकैः ॥ ६२ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: One who at the time of death drinks water in which a rudrākṣa has been pressed, thinking of Rudra, goes to Rudra's world.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: मृत्युकाले च रुद्राक्षं निष्पीड्य सह वारिणा । यः पिबेच्चिन्तयन् रुद्रं रुद्रलोकं स गच्छति ॥ ६४ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: As there is no principle greater than Śiva, there is no mantra greater than the five-syllable mantra; when it is known, what fruit is there in other mantras, as when Śiva, root of the world, is known, what fruit in other gods? Among seven crore mantras the five-syllable is great, as Śambhu is greater than Brahmā, Viṣṇu and the gods.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: Maheśvara, the supreme self, is the cause of all worlds; this mantra is his designation and the one cause of all mantras; since it is his name and he is what it names, the supreme Śiva is established through the mantra. One says 'namaḥ' first and then 'śivāya' — this five-syllable mantra stands at the head of all the śrutis.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: Śambhu, dense with consciousness and bliss, is called Śiva because he is pure from the beginning, free of the three impurities, and the abode of all auspicious things; the two syllables 'Śi-va' reveal the supreme brahman in their primary sense, while other words apply only secondarily — hence 'Śiva' is the foremost name.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: All the five elements, five subtle elements, five sense and five action organs, the five brahmas and the five acts with their causes are to be understood through the five syllables; everything that exists in fives is made of the five-syllable mantra.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: Preceded by Oṃ this mantra is called the six-syllable mantra in the Śaiva Āgamas and the Vedas; the single syllable praṇava reveals the partless, second-less Śiva; the mantra of the supreme self is of the form 'so'ham', and by dropping its 'h' and 's' the one-syllable Oṃ arises; the praṇava reveals the partless (niṣkala) Śiva, the five-syllable the Śiva embodied in the five brahmas, and Śiva, who is both, abides in the six-syllable.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: Japa is threefold — spoken, whispered and mental: spoken, heard by those nearby with its syllables distinct; whispered, with lips barely touching; mental, contemplated inwardly in the form of the syllables without moving lips or tongue; all sacrifices, vows, gifts and austerities are not worth a sixteenth of the sacrifice of japa, and the mental japa of this mantra is the best, destroying terrible saṃsāra.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: Those who live on water or on air and others emaciated by vows do not reach Śiva's world by those vows; austerities, sacrifices, vows and observances are not equal to a crore-part of worship with the five syllables; the impure or pure, even the fallen, who worships once with it is freed; the Agnihotra, the three Vedas and sacrifices with rich fees are not equal to a crore-part of its japa.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse. Also the text's own rejection of extreme fasting vows as a path to Śiva (8.36).

paraphrase: Hearing, singing, remembering Śambhu, serving his feet, worship, salutation, servitude, friendship and self-offering — thus the ninefold devotion taught by the god Śambhu, hard for sinners to find and easy for those of meritorious deeds.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: श्रवणं कीर्तनं शम्भोः स्मरणं पादसेवनम् । अर्चनं वन्दनं दास्यं सख्यमात्मनिवेदनम् ॥ २ ॥ एवं नवविधा भक्तिः प्रोक्ता देवेन शम्भुना । दुर्लभा पापिनां लोके सुलभा पुण्यकर्मणाम् ॥ ३ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: Wherever, in the low or the high, Śaṅkara's devotion is strong, that one is sung as a bhakta; the one in whom devotion is made firm, be he a mleccha or the best of the twice-born, is dear to Śambhu and is a vipra; one without devotion is not dear.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: अधमे चोत्तमे वापि यत्र कुत्रचिदूर्जिता । वर्तते शाङ्करी भक्तिः स भक्त इति गीयते ॥ ४ ॥ भक्तिः स्थिरीकृता यस्मिन्म्लेच्छे वा द्विजसत्तमे । शम्भोः प्रियः सविप्रश्च न प्रियो भक्तिवर्जितः ॥ ५ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: Devotion is outer (gross) and inner (subtle), and the Vīramāheśvaras honour the inner: to set the breath in Śambhu's liṅga and the liṅga in the breath, make the mind steady and think of nothing — this the Śivayogins call inner devotion; the life of one in whom it abides is like a burnt seed.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: That devotion comes from grace, and grace arises from devotion, as the seed from the sprout and the sprout from the seed; the devotion preceded by grace that gives liberation cannot be obtained by humans in a single birth.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: प्रसादादेव सा भक्तिः प्रसादो भक्तिसम्भवः । यथैवाङ्कुरतो बीजं बीजतो वा यथाङ्कुरः ॥ ११ ॥ प्रसादपूर्विका येयं भक्तिर्मुक्तिविधायिनी । नैव सा शक्यते प्राप्तुं नरैरेकेन जन्मना ॥ १२ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: Worship is fivefold — austerity, action, japa, meditation and knowledge: austerity is drying the body for Śiva, not the kṛcchra penances; action is Śiva's worship, not outer sacrifices; japa is practice of the five syllables, the praṇava or the Rudrādhyāya, not Veda-recitation; knowledge is understanding the meaning of the Śiva Āgamas, not other learning — this is the fivefold Śiva-sacrifice.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: The glorious devotee of Śiva should not touch, look at, or ever live with those averse to Śiva-devotion; from the time of initiation with the wearing of the liṅga, the devotee should honour those who stand in his own Āgama.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: शिवभक्तो महातेजाः शिवभक्तिपराङ्मुखान् । न स्पृशेन्नैव वीक्षेत न तैः सह वसेत् क्वचित् ॥ २७ ॥ यदा दीक्षाप्रवेशःस्याल्लिङ्गधारणपूर्वकः । तदाप्रभृति भक्तोऽसौ पूजयेत् स्वागमस्थितान् ॥ २८ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: He should eat in the houses of twice-born of his own jāti who are devoted to the conduct of his own path, and never in others' houses.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse. A commensality rule within the Sanskrit Pañcācārya strand; contrast the vacanas.

original.text: स्वमार्गाचारनिरताः सजातीया द्विजास्तु ये । तेषां गृहेषु भुञ्जीत नेतरेषां कदाचन ॥ २९ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: All goods sent by bhavis — worldlings averse to the conduct of the path — are to be given up; the firm devotee should not worship, remember or praise other gods, nor eat what is offered to them, and should leave houses where another god is kept.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: For those steadfast in Śiva alone on the Vīraśaiva way, the leavings (nirmālya) of fixed liṅgas are not to be used; where harm befalls fixed liṅgas or Śiva's devotees who bear his marks, one should prevent it even at the cost of one's life, and one who gives up life for Śiva attains union with him.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: On seeing a reviler of Śiva one should have him killed or curse him, or, if unable, leave that place.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse. Textual background of gaṇācāra (defence of the faith); recorded as the text states it.

original.text: शिवनिन्दाकरं दृष्ट्वा घातयेदथवा शपेत् । स्थानं वा तत्परित्यज्य गच्छेद् यद्यक्षमो भवेत् ॥ ३६ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: Having become devoted to Śiva's worship one should let go of prior ritual karma, or else that worship becomes fruitless; one who has taken the higher way and resorts to a lower practice is known as 'fallen after ascending' (ārūḍhapatita), excluded from all rites.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: शिवपूजापरो भूत्वा पूर्वकर्म विसर्जयेत् । अथवा पूर्वकर्म स्यात् सा पूजा निष्फला भवेत् ॥ ३९ ॥ उत्तमां गतिमाश्रित्य नीचां वृत्तिं समाश्रितः । आरूढपतितो ज्ञेयः सर्वकर्मबहिष्कृतः ॥ ४० ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: The bhakta skilled in pure, innate giving, intent on Śiva and turned away from the stations of Brahmā and the others is called māheśvara; when devotion rises to excellence through the weight of dispassion, the bhakta with steady discernment is called māheśvara.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: केवले सहजे दाने निष्णातः शिवतत्परः । ब्रह्मादिस्थानविमुखो भक्तो माहेश्वरः स्मृतः ॥ २ ॥ भक्तेर्यदा समुत्कर्षो भवेद् वैराग्यगौरवात् । तदा माहेश्वरः प्रोक्तो भक्तः स्थिरविवेकवान् ॥ ३ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: The great sthala of steadfastness in the liṅga is taught for the māheśvara, maintained even at the loss of life: let all one has be taken, let one's head be cut off — the māheśvara does not let go of the great vow of liṅga-worship.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: अस्य माहेश्वरस्योक्तं लिङ्गनिष्ठामहास्थलम् । प्राणात्ययेऽपि सम्पन्ने यदत्याज्यं विधीयते ॥ २१ ॥ अपगच्छतु सर्वस्वं शिरश्छेदनमस्तु वा । माहेश्वरो न मुञ्चेत लिङ्गपूजामहाव्रतम् ॥ २२ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: What need has the one steadfast in the liṅga of karma that leads to heaven, when the śāstras declare his attainment of Śiva, eternal bliss?
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: लिङ्गनिष्ठस्य किं तस्य कर्मणा स्वर्गहेतुना । नित्यानन्दशिवप्राप्तिर्यस्य शास्त्रेषु निश्चिता ॥ २८ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: The māheśvara, his heart set on the liṅga alone, should give up the dharmas of his former station that obstruct his conduct; giving up the dharmas born of his own jāti and family that oppose steadfastness in the liṅga, he is known as the rejecter of the former station.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: लिङ्गैकनिष्ठहृदयः सदा माहेश्वरो जनः । पूर्वाश्रयगतान् धर्मांस्त्यज्येत् स्वाचाररोधकान् ॥ ३० ॥ स्वजातिकुलजान् धर्मान् लिङ्गनिष्ठाविरोधिनः । त्यजन् माहेश्वरो ज्ञेयः पूर्वाश्रयनिरासकः ॥ ३१ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: Humans are of two kinds, the purified and the ordinary (prākṛta): those who have received Śiva's sacraments are pure, the others ordinary; the ordering of the dharmas of varṇa and āśrama is twofold, one taught by Śiva and the other by Brahmā: steadfastness in Śiva's dharma belongs to those who dwell in Śiva's āśrama, while for those without Śiva's sacraments the dharma of the Grandfather is laid down.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: Because worship and its acts cannot be accomplished without difference between the worshipped and the worshipper — the liṅga and the jīva — and because such non-difference opposes steadfastness in the liṅga, and because the knowledge that would ground a total non-duality is absent at this stage, the māheśvara, a man of ritual action, is the rejecter of total non-duality (sarvādvaita).
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: पूज्यपूजकयोर्लिङ्गजीवयोर्भेदवर्जने । पूजाकर्माद्यसम्पत्तेर्लिङ्गनिष्ठाविरोधतः ॥ ३७ ॥ सर्वाद्वैतविचारस्य ज्ञानाभावो व्यवस्थितेः । भवेन्माहेश्वरः कर्मी सर्वाद्वैतनिरासकः ॥ ३८ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: The Lord (pati) is Mahādeva himself; the bound soul (paśu) depends on him; if the two were not different, how could they be master and servant?
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: पतिः साक्षान्महादेवः पशुरेष तदाश्रयः । अनयोः स्वामिभृत्यत्वमभेदे कथमिष्यते ॥ ४० ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: When the supreme principle is directly realized through awakening, then non-duality is attained; never for one without knowledge.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: साक्षात्कृतं परं तत्त्वं यदा भवति बोधतः । तदाद्वैतसमापत्तिर्ज्ञानहीनस्य न क्वचित् ॥ ४१ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: Because difference is the ground of action, everyday practice proceeds; one engaged in the acts of liṅga-worship should not practise non-duality — worship always rests on difference, so the one devoted to liṅga-worship should not be intent on non-duality.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: भेदस्य कर्महेतुत्वाद् व्यवहारः प्रवर्तते । लिङ्गपूजादिकर्मस्थो न चाद्वैतं समाचरेत् ॥ ४२ ॥ पूजादिव्यवहारः स्याद्भेदाश्रयतया सदा । लिङ्गपूजापरस्तस्मान्नाद्वैते निरतो भवेत् ॥ ४३ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: The one devoted to liṅga-worship does not invoke Śiva into his own chosen liṅga: from the moment the great guru gives the liṅga filled with Śiva's power, Śiva abides in it — what invocation then? Śiva is always present in sacramentally consecrated liṅgas, so invocation, which contradicts this understanding, is not to be done; neither invocation nor dismissal in one's own liṅga — this is the settled view of the śāstra.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: As the oneness of self and Śiva is not held by one bound to action, so non-duality of earth and the other elements with Śiva is not accepted: the Lord's eightfold form is taught in the sense that he presides over them; all this, earth and the rest, is effect and Maheśvara the agent — as the potter is not the clay; the eightfold world from earth to the self is the Lord's body, and between this body and the god who is its self there is neither non-difference nor separate existence.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: If Maheśa's all-pervasiveness meant worship everywhere, one would not be steadfast in the liṅga; though all-pervading, Śambhu abides especially in his own support, so, turned away from elsewhere, one should worship Śiva in one's own chosen liṅga — he is manifest there intensely, as fire is especially found within śamī wood.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: Since this moving and unmoving world arose from Mahādeva, it is not different from him, as pots from clay, as foam, waves and bubbles from the ocean, as cloth made of threads; all this world is made of Śiva and shines as non-different from him — like the snake in the rope, silver in the shell, a thief in a post, water in a mirage, a gandharva city in the sky — in Śiva who is being, consciousness and bliss and free of difference; as a tree stands in the form of leaves and branches, the one Śiva shines in the form of earth and the rest.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse. The passage uses both transformation images (clay, threads) and appearance images (rope-snake).

paraphrase: Though the self of the whole world, the supreme lord Śaṅkara shines especially in the lotus hearts of his devotees — as on Kailāsa, Mandara, Himālaya and Meru — and as the all-self is delimited in bodies, so Śaṅkara is in his own devotees.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: His bonds of sin destroyed through steadfastness in the liṅga and the rest, he is called prasādī through the attainment of serenity of mind (manaḥ-prasāda).
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: लिङ्गनिष्ठादिभावेन ध्वस्तपापनिबन्धनः । मनःप्रसादयोगेन प्रसादीत्येष कथ्यते ॥ २ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: Purity of mind is the mark of prasāda and is achieved only by the grace of Śiva in the form of the liṅga; what is offered to Śiva is his prasāda, the nirmālya that makes the mind pure; by purity of food comes purity of the principles; whatever is set aside for one's own enjoyment is to be offered to the god first and then eaten, for self-purification.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: The guru is the cause of all accomplishment, for Mahādeva stands present in the form of the guru: the partless Mahādeva, ocean of eternal knowledge, becomes with parts as the guru to bless all.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: गुरुरेवात्र सर्वेषां कारणं सिद्धिकर्मणाम् । गुरुरूपो महादेवो यतः साक्षादुपस्थितः ॥ १९ ॥ निष्कलो हि महादेवो नित्यज्ञानमहोदधिः । सकलो गुरुरूपेण सर्वानुग्राहको भवेत् ॥ २० ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: Who is Śiva is to be known as the guru; who is the guru is remembered as Śiva; the wise make no difference between them in gaining knowledge.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: यः शिवः स गुरुर्ज्ञेयो यो गुरुः स शिवः स्मृतः । न तयोरन्तरं कुर्याद् ज्ञानावाप्तौ महामतिः ॥ २१ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: One should not call the knowledge-giving ācārya, who abides as Śiva, equal to others because he has hands and feet like theirs; disrespect to the ācārya destroys the attainment of the good; without devotion to the guru, devotion to Śiva does not arise — as to Śiva, so to the guru.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: The pedestal is the supreme Śakti, the liṅga is the supreme Śiva himself; the union of Śiva and Śakti — the universe — is called the liṅga.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: पीठिका परमा शक्तिर्लिङ्गं साक्षात् परः शिवः । शिवशक्तिसमायोगं विश्वं लिङ्गं तदुच्यते ॥ ३२ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: Those who see the web of the world as consciousness through Śiva-yoga, untouched by impurity, are Śivayogins: they have conquered desire and anger, split the knot of delusion, regard clod, stone and gold as equal, are the same to foe and friend, free of longing and ego; where the dust of their feet falls, that house is holy; to see them gives accomplishment, to touch them quiets sin, to worship them is a means of liberation.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: What are Vedas, what śāstras, sacrifices, austerities and vows, if embodied beings sick with birth have no devotion to Śaṅkara? Even the good works of one without Śiva-devotion are fruitless or yield the opposite, as at Dakṣa's great sacrifice.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: किं वेदैः किं ततः शास्त्रैः किं यज्ञैः किं तपोव्रतैः । नास्ति चेच्छाङ्करी भक्तिर्देहिनां जन्मरोगिणाम् ॥ ४८ ॥ शिवभक्तिविहीनस्य सुकृतं चापि निष्फलम् । विपरीतफलं च स्याद् दक्षस्यापि महाध्वरे ॥ ४९ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: The one called bhakta, māheśvara and prasādī is so called through the predominance of action; now his yoga of knowledge is told: the liṅga is brahman of the nature of consciousness, its power has the form of the breath (prāṇa); one who knows the liṅga of that form is called prāṇaliṅgī.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: भक्तो माहेश्वरश्चैष प्रसादीति च कीर्तितः । कर्मप्राधान्ययोगेन ज्ञानयोगोऽस्य कथ्यते ॥ २ ॥ लिङ्गं चिदात्मकं ब्रह्म तच्छक्तिः प्राणरूपिणी । तद्रूपलिङ्गविज्ञानी प्राणलिङ्गीति कथ्यते ॥ ३ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: What arises from the middle of the bulb (kanda) through the meeting of prāṇa and apāna is called the prāṇaliṅga by those who restrain prāṇa and apāna; that in which the breath dissolves like frost in the sun is the prāṇaliṅga, and its bearer takes its form; the liṅga of supreme brahman, of the form of consciousness, shines like a lamp within those who know and are joined in yoga, and is not contemplated by the ignorant.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse. The commentary specifies that the breath practice is done on the teacher's instruction; no method is recorded here.

paraphrase: Those who abandon the supreme liṅga standing within, of the nature of light and of Śiva, and stay with the outer liṅga are called deluded; the yogin who always reflects on the liṅga of awareness, turned away from outer things, is called prāṇaliṅgī.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: अन्तःस्थितं परं लिङ्गं ज्योतीरूपं शिवात्मकम् । विहाय बाह्यलिङ्गस्था विमूढा इति कीर्तिताः ॥ ९ ॥ संविल्लिङ्गपरामर्शी बाह्यवस्तुपराङ्मुखः । यः सदा वर्तते योगी प्राणलिङ्गी स उच्यते ॥ १० ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: Worshipping the inner liṅga of consciousness with flowers of feeling is prāṇaliṅga-worship: seated in the heart-shrine lit by the lamp of awareness, the nine doors of the senses shut, cooled by nectar from the moon at the crown, one should worship the liṅga of consciousness with offerings of feeling — forbearance its bathing water, discrimination its cloth, truth its ornament, dispassion its garland, the wealth of samādhi its scent, freedom from ego its unbroken rice, faith its incense, great knowledge its lamp, the world rooted in delusion its food offering, silence its bell, the offering of sense-objects its betel, freedom from sense-delusion its circumambulation, and the intellect's power one with That its prostration.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: For one intent on inner action, the attainment of meditation on Śiva as the self through the stages of prāṇaliṅga-worship is called samādhi: one should contemplate the supreme self — above all principles, radiant with being, consciousness and bliss, self-luminous, beyond speech and mind, lit by the great power named Umā — in the form of the haṃsa with the feeling 'I am He' (so'ham); the attainment of undivided attention on That is the supreme samādhi; the great liṅga is the supreme brahman and the breath is the jīva — by contemplating their oneness one is established in samādhi.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: One should contemplate within the lotuses mounted on the six centres, from the base to between the brows, the seats of Brahmā and the others; above the brows the thousand-petalled lotus, and in it the stainless moon-disc; know the subtle aperture within it, called the abode of Kailāsa, and contemplate there Śambhu, cause of all causes.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: Some say the liṅga is the unmanifest (avyakta), the root cause of the worlds, and Maheśvara the bearer of the liṅga — this view is incoherent.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: अव्यक्तं लिङ्गमित्याहुर्जगतां मूलकारणम् । लिङ्गी महेश्वरश्चेति मतमेतदसङ्गतम् ॥ ३७ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: Neither sun nor moon shines there, nor lightning, fire or stars, where the great liṅga, the supreme self, is shining; śruti calls the supreme liṅga luminous and of Śiva's nature, by whose light all this shines; there is no principle higher than the liṅga, from which the world is born, whose form it takes and into which it dissolves; therefore by meditating on the liṅga — supreme brahman, being-consciousness-bliss — as one's own form, that state arises.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse. 12.38 echoes Kaṭha Upaniṣad 5.15 / Muṇḍaka 2.2.10 / Śvetāśvatara 6.14.

paraphrase: They call knowledge the aṅga and the eternal knowable the liṅga; one who has both is called aṅgaliṅgī: the liṅga mounted on the aṅga and the aṅga present in the liṅga — one who has both is aṅgaliṅgavān; one who, knowing the liṅga within himself as light, always worships and contemplates it is the aṅgaliṅgī.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: One whose mind is settled in 'this liṅga is liberation itself' is liberated even while joined to a body; he is a knower, a great guru.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: मुक्तिरूपमिदं लिङ्गमिति यस्य मनःस्थितिः । स मुक्तो देहयोगेऽपि स ज्ञानी स महागुरुः ॥ ४६ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: The aṅgaliṅgī, whose form is knowledge, is to be known as the wife (satī) and Śiva as the husband (pati); one who has the bliss of their union is named śaraṇa.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: अङ्गलिङ्गी ज्ञानरूपः सती ज्ञेयः शिवः पतिः । यत्सौख्यं तत्समावेशे तद्वान् शरणनामवान् ॥ २ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: One who contemplates his power in Śiva as a faithful wife in her beloved, turned from all else, is known as śaraṇa; when Śiva is directly known, who desires another? Having found a great treasure, who begs glass from others? Having reached Śiva's bliss, who serves another? Leaving the nectar of the Gaṅgā, who would long for a mirage?
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: How can the elephants of desire, anger, great delusion, pride and envy stay near the lion of Śiva-knowledge? One who hates anything anywhere in the world, which has Śiva's form, is a hater of Śiva, his mind possessed by rajas; one who hates all people, always makes 'I', and is given to untrue notions is tāmasa.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: Without a perfected guru how can saṃsāra be undone — how would a disease go without a physician who knows its cause? The best guru is the one who cleanses the mirror of the mind soiled by ignorance with the wealth of wisdom; gurus devoted to Śiva-non-duality, wish-fulfilling trees of liberation and abodes of compassion, are rare in this world.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: Inquiry into the principle of Śiva is called śīla; śīla is steadiness of feeling in Śaṅkara, remover of the afflictions of those who take refuge; it is sole knowledge of Śiva, one-pointed meditation on him and longing to reach him; as a faithful wife's conduct is praised for love of her husband, so one is of good śīla through love for Śiva; in short, single steadfastness in the knowledge of Śiva is śīla.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: The one named śaraṇa, having reached surpassing bliss through union with the prāṇaliṅga and the rest, becomes one in union (aikya) through contemplating oneness with Śiva.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: प्राणलिङ्गादियोगेन सुखातिशयमेयिवान् । शरणाख्यः शिवेनैक्यभावनादैक्यवान् भवेत् ॥ २ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: Free of longing for the droplets of sense-pleasure, pure of intent, by immersion in the great ocean of Śiva's bliss — this is called union (aikya).
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: विषयानन्दकणिकानिस्पृहो निर्मलाशयः । शिवानन्दमहासिन्धुमज्जनादैक्यमुच्यते ॥ ४ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: With the bond of impurity shaken off and the mind stainless, by the feeling 'I am Śiva' he is established in oneness with Śiva; one who has attained oneness with Śiva, whose form is consciousness and bliss, does not see the net of the world, a display fashioned by māyā; the ocean of māyā, with its principle-waves and bubbling cosmic eggs, dissolves in the submarine fire of oneness with Śiva.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: Difference in Śiva is imagined through the concealment wrought by the power of māyā; when that is destroyed for the self, nothing but non-duality is accepted; being a bound soul (paśu) and being the Lord (pati) are imagined by māyā's delusion — when that dissolves, who is paśu and who is pati?
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: मायाशक्तितिरोधानाच्छिवे भेदविकल्पना । आत्मनस्तद्विनाशे तु नाद्वैतात्किञ्चिदिष्यते ॥ ८ ॥ पशुत्वं च पतित्वं च मायामोहविकल्पितम् । तस्मिन् प्रलयमापन्ने कः पशुः को नु वा पतिः ॥ ९ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: For the dreadful serpent of saṃsāra lying in the anthill of difference, the contemplation of supreme non-duality is the remedy; the teacher crosses the great ocean of saṃsāra born of the sense of difference in the boat of non-dual understanding; the night of saṃsāra is destroyed by the sun of non-duality; for yogins there is no means like non-dual contemplation to end saṃsāra's burning; the bliss born of it in a single moment is not obtained by enjoyers in a crore of years.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: For the Śivayogin in whom the world has dissolved into the mind's activity, the upsurge of Śiva's bliss is called liberation (mukti).
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: चित्तवृत्तिसमालीनजगतः शिवयोगिनः । शिवानन्दपरिस्फूर्तिर्मुक्तिरित्यभिधीयते ॥ १५ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: The teacher who has become Śiva through sole contemplation of Śiva is, though embodied, not tainted by his own conduct nor by birth- and death-pollution and the like.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: शिवैकभावनापन्नशिवत्वो देहवानपि । देशिको हि न लिप्येत स्वाचारैः सूतकादिभिः ॥ १६ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: When knowledge of Śiva's non-duality is firm, what is to be done by actions performed or not performed? Seeing everywhere equally through the oneness of Śambhu, even doing great deeds he does not reap their fruit.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: शिवाद्वैतपरिज्ञाने स्थिते सति मनस्विनाम् । कर्मणां किं नु भाव्यं स्यादकृतेन कृतेन वा ॥ १७ ॥ शम्भोरेकत्वभावेन सर्वत्र समदर्शनः । कुर्वन्नपि महाकर्म न तत्फलमवाप्नुयात् ॥ १८ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: Meritorious or sinful, brāhmaṇa or outcaste — among those joined in the one contemplation of Śiva he surely becomes alike; what use has the knower for the good conduct of varṇa and āśrama? Yet worldly good conduct is still observed, even without fruit.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: सुकृती दुष्कृती वापि ब्राह्मणो वान्त्यजोऽपि वा । शिवैकभावयुक्तानां सदृशो भवति ध्रुवम् ॥ १९ ॥ वर्णाश्रमसदाचारैर्ज्ञानिना किं प्रयोजनम् । लौकिकस्तु सदाचारः फलाभावेऽपि भाव्यते ॥ २० ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: For one whose seeds of karma are burnt by the fire of stainless knowledge and who appears as if embodied, the body's journey is merely worldly; established in Śiva-knowledge and firm dispassion he is not tainted by his acts, as a lotus leaf by water; walking, standing, sleeping or waking he is always intent on Śiva's worship; whatever he sees is the vision of Śiva, whatever he thinks is meditation on Śiva, and every movement of the Śivayogins is Maheśa's worship.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: Always contemplating the universe as made of Śiva, because his self is the one vessel of Śiva he is called 'one-vessel' (ekabhājana): seeing the non-duality of himself, all the world and Śiva; the world is in Śiva and Śiva shines everywhere; for one whose mind's single vessel is consciousness, what is there in things rooted in māyā? The yogin who always abides in his heart, empty of mental activity, dissolved in Śiva and untroubled, is liberated — there is no doubt.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: Remembering guru, Śiva and disciple as one's own nature, through the feeling that oneself consumes all, is called eating together (sahabhojana): one should always join Śiva, the universe and the guru in oneself as one in the form of consciousness; one who no longer has the notion 'this is Śiva, this the guru, this the moving and unmoving world, and this I' is the enjoyer of all.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: One who no longer thinks 'I am the servant, Śiva the master; I am the disciple, he the guru' is established in the state of non-duality.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: अहं भृत्यः शिवः स्वामी शिष्योऽहं गुरुरेव वै । इति यस्य मतिर्नास्ति स चाद्वैतपदे स्थितः ॥ ३७ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: Offering the oblation of 'this-ness' (idantā) into the fire of one's own self, full of supreme I-ness and illumining the universe, one is called the offerer of the universe; the knowledge by which one rightly knows 'I am Śiva, I am the guru, I am the whole moving and unmoving world' is called full I-ness (pūrṇāhantā); the knowledge-sacrificer who offers the world, the mass of difference, as oblation into the fire of the ground of consciousness is the eater of the universe's oblation; for those whose mental activity has dissolved into the supreme sky of consciousness, what order of the world remains?
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: In the stainless sky of consciousness, free of the world's obstruction, one should contemplate the self as dissolved, by the nature of equal flavour (sāmarasya); this is the supreme knowledge, illumining being and bliss, called liberation by the good, ending the world's delusion; through the practice of the dharmas offered in the stations beginning with bhakta, having attained oneness with the wondrous Śiva who is the sky of consciousness, one becomes a vessel of the glory of liberation.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: For one endowed in due order with the good conduct taught in the six sthalas, the liṅga-sthalas are now told, which are aimed at liberation while living: fifty-seven divisions from the guru to the void of knowledge, resting on the sthalas from bhakta onward.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: That by which supreme knowledge is given and the bondage of fetters is destroyed is dīkṣā; the guru in it is remembered as the guru of initiation.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: दीयते परमं ज्ञानं क्षीयते पाशबन्धनम् । यया दीक्षेति सा तस्यां गुरुर्दीक्षागुरुः स्मृतः ॥ ७ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: 'Gu' is what is beyond the qualities and 'ru' what is beyond form — one who gives that which is beyond the qualities and formless is called guru; because he gathers the meanings of the śāstras, establishes others in conduct and himself practises it, he is called ācārya.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: गुणातीतं गुकारं च रूपातीतं रुकारकम् । गुणातीतमरूपं च यो दद्यात् स गुरुः स्मृतः ॥ ८ ॥ आचिनोति च शास्त्रार्थानाचारे स्थापयत्यलम् । स्वयमाचरते यस्मादाचार्यस्तेन चोच्यते ॥ ९ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: Where action dissolves through the guru's knowledge is called the liṅga of action; the liṅga alone is the supreme light, brahman itself, so by its worship alone the fruit of all rites arises; yogins, giving up all rites, are devoted solely to liṅga-worship; sacrifices and all rites equal only a fraction of liṅga-worship — what are sacrifices like the Agnihotra and hard austerities to one whose delight is liṅga-worship? He is accomplished in all rites.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: Where feeling (bhāva) dissolves as action did is the bhāvaliṅga: the supreme Śiva is grasped by feeling, and, eternally full, is pleased through the devotees' feeling; the bhāvaliṅga excels the liṅga made of clay or stone; one who, leaving outer liṅgas, remembers the liṅga of consciousness in the mind and worships it with flowers of feeling is a bhāvaliṅgī — worshipping the lamp-like liṅga at the base, in the mind or between the brows, he no longer worships a liṅga of stone, clay or wood; ritual worship is for those of little understanding, inner worship for the knowers.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: Śiva is supreme and his worship is called action; since the Āgamas are devoted to it, this is the 'Āgama of action'; as fire does not appear in the kindling wood without churning, so Śiva within does not shine without action; one should act so that no rule is broken and the god is pleased, with the Āgama as authority.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: Because he blesses the worlds by showing his own body, he is named 'blessing through the body': as Śiva blesses embodied beings by entering a form, so the yogin abiding in the body becomes a blesser of all; and as Śiva is unattached though joined to a body, so the yogin in the body always remains unattached.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

paraphrase: When, giving up the state of the jīva, the principle is contemplated through the guru's teaching, this is called the self (ātman): dwelling in the heart, like the hundredth part of a hair-tip, not eating the fruit of karma, the self shines like a lamp; yet the self of all beings, resting in the inner organ, has become atomic through contact with impurity and is governed by the beginningless karma.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse. 18.6 echoes Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad 5.9.

paraphrase: The knowledge by which duality between guru and disciple is removed through initiation — the oneness of their bliss — is called the 'foot-water of initiation'; or 'foot' (pāda) means the guru and 'water' (udaka) the disciple, and their oneness comes through initiation.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: दीक्षयाऽपगतद्वैतं यज्ज्ञानं गुरुशिष्ययोः । आनन्दस्यैक्यमेतेन दीक्षापादोदकं स्मृतम् ॥ ६ ॥ अथवा पादशब्देन गुरुरेव निगद्यते । शिष्यश्चोदकशब्देन तयोरैक्यं तु दीक्षया ॥ ७ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: In the self of consciousness, where there is neither primary nor secondary meaning, his acceptance of grace is unfettered; having attained the direct realization of awareness that plays through the dealings of knower, known and means of knowing, the yogin abides in his own self.
speaker: Reṇuka
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: मुख्यार्थो लक्षणार्थश्च यत्र नास्ति चिदात्मनि । विशृङ्खलतया तस्य प्रसादः स्वीकृतो भवेत् ॥ ६ ॥ मातृमेयप्रमाणादिव्यवहारे विहारिणीम् । संवित्साक्षात्कृतिं लब्ध्वा योगी स्वात्मनि तिष्ठति ॥ ७ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: Having spoken, Reṇuka vanished before his eyes, meditating on Mahādeva within; whoever hears with a pure mind this Śiva-siddhānta, the supreme Vīraśaiva doctrine, reaches the highest state.
speaker: narrator
notes: Ref and wording checked against the local e-text (Muktabodha M00207); paraphrase by U20 from the verse.

original.text: इत्युक्त्वा पश्यतस्तस्य पुरस्तादेव रेणुकः । अन्तर्दधे महादेवं चिन्तयन्नन्तरात्मना ॥ १ ॥ य इदं शिवसिद्धान्तं वीरशैवमतं परम् । शृणोति शुद्धमनसा स याति परमां गतिम् ॥ २ ॥
original.edition: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

paraphrase: The rich will make temples for Śiva; what shall I, a poor man, do? My legs are the pillars, my body the shrine, my head the golden cupola. Listen, Kūḍalasaṅgamadēva: the standing (sthāvara) shall perish, the moving (jaṅgama) shall not.
speaker: Basava
notes: Skeleton from memory; locator is the incipit (or a descriptive key when the incipit is not recalled) because vacana numbering differs between editions — fix against the Samagra Vacana Sāhitya in Phase D. Among the most quoted vacanas; A. K. Ramanujan's Speaking of Śiva numbers it 820 (his edition's numbering; low confidence on the number).

paraphrase: Do not steal, do not kill, do not lie, do not rage, do not be disgusted with others, do not praise yourself, do not blame others: this is inner purity, this is outer purity; this is the way to please our Kūḍalasaṅgamadēva.
speaker: Basava

paraphrase: What kind of dharma is it that has no compassion? Compassion is needed toward all living beings; compassion is the root of dharma; the Lord of the meeting rivers accepts nothing without it.
speaker: Basava
notes: Skeleton from memory; locator is the incipit (or a descriptive key when the incipit is not recalled) because vacana numbering differs between editions — fix against the Samagra Vacana Sāhitya in Phase D.

paraphrase: Let me not say of a devotee 'Whose is he? whose is he?' — let me say 'He is ours, ours, ours'; Kūḍalasaṅgamadēva, make me known as a son of your house.

notes: Skeleton from memory; locator is the incipit (or a descriptive key when the incipit is not recalled) because vacana numbering differs between editions — fix against the Samagra Vacana Sāhitya in Phase D.

paraphrase: I will put the Veda to the touchstone, put the śāstras in fetters, flog the back of logic and cut off the nose of the Āgamas; see, great giver Kūḍalasaṅgamadēva — I am the son in the house of Mādāra Cennayya.
speaker: Basava
notes: Skeleton from memory; locator is the incipit (or a descriptive key when the incipit is not recalled) because vacana numbering differs between editions — fix against the Samagra Vacana Sāhitya in Phase D.

paraphrase: When they see a snake of stone they pour milk on it; when they see a real snake they say 'Kill it!'; to the devotee of the god, who could eat, they say 'Go away'; to the god's image, which cannot eat, they offer food.
speaker: Basava
notes: Skeleton from memory; locator is the incipit (or a descriptive key when the incipit is not recalled) because vacana numbering differs between editions — fix against the Samagra Vacana Sāhitya in Phase D.

paraphrase: Lord, do not make me say 'I am He' (sōhaṃ); make me say 'I am your servant' (dāsōhaṃ).
speaker: Basava
notes: Skeleton from memory; locator is the incipit (or a descriptive key when the incipit is not recalled) because vacana numbering differs between editions — fix against the Samagra Vacana Sāhitya in Phase D. paraphrase: When one speaks, the words should be like a string of pearls, like the lustre of a ruby, like a shaft of crystal, so that the Liṅga itself says 'Yes, yes'; if one's deeds do not match one's words, how will Kūḍalasaṅgama be pleased?
speaker: Basava

paraphrase: Before the grey reaches the cheek and the wrinkle the chin, before the body becomes a cage of bones, before the teeth fall and the back bends and you lean on others — worship the Lord of the meeting rivers.

paraphrase: They say gold is māyā — gold is not māyā; they say woman is māyā — woman is not māyā; they say land is māyā — land is not māyā; the desire standing before the mind is māyā, O Guhēśvara.

paraphrase: Millions died of desire, millions of greed, millions for gold, woman and land; O Guhēśvara, I see none who died for you.

paraphrase: Like the silkworm that builds its house out of its own love and dies wound round and round in its own threads, I burn with the desires of my heart; Lord, cut through my heart's greed and show me the way out, Cennamallikārjuna.

paraphrase: Having built a house on the hill, why fear the beasts? Having built a house on the seashore, why fear the waves? Having built a house in the market, why be ashamed of noise? Born into the world, when praise and blame come one must not get angry but stay calm, Cennamallikārjuna.

paraphrase: I love the Beautiful One who has no death, no decay and no form, no place, no end, no birth; I love him, mother; Cennamallikārjuna is my husband — take these husbands who die and decay and feed them to your kitchen fires.
speaker: Akka Mahādēvi
